Note::split_lines¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

TokenBatch Note::split_lines() const
TokenBatch Note::split_lines(bool keep_ends) const

Split Each Cell Into Lines¶

split_lines() breaks each text cell at line terminators and returns the lines as a TokenBatch. Reach for it when the cells hold multi-line content — prompts, templates, markdown, copied terminal output, document sections — and you want line-level structure.

A line terminator is \n, a lone \r, or the pair \r\n (consumed as a single break). By default the terminators are removed from the returned line tokens; split_lines(true) keeps each line’s terminator attached (a \r\n line keeps both bytes), which is what you want if you intend to rejoin the lines and reproduce the original exactly.

Trailing terminator and blank lines¶

A terminator at the very end of a cell ends the last line rather than starting an empty one, so "a\nb\n" yields two lines, not three. A blank line in the middle is a real empty line and is kept: "a\n\nc" yields "a", "", "c". An empty cell yields no lines at all.

The TokenBatch result¶

All lines from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run: cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). A cell that produced no lines contributes an empty range.

Example 1: Basic Line Split¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"line1\nline2\nline3", "solo"}).split_lines();

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["line1", "line2", "line3", "solo"]
offsets: [0, 3, 4]

Example 2: A Trailing Newline Adds No Empty Line¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a\nb\n"}).split_lines();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b"]

Example 3: A Blank Line In The Middle Is Kept¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a\n\nc"}).split_lines();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["a", "", "c"]

Example 4: \r\n Is One Break¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a\r\nb"}).split_lines();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b"]

The \r and \n are consumed together; neither remains in a token.

Example 5: Keeping The Terminators¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a\nb\n"}).split_lines(true);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a\n", "b\n"]

Each line keeps its \n (shown by print as the escape \n).

Example 6: An Empty Cell Produces No Lines¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({""}).split_lines();

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets: [0, 0]

The one input cell maps to the empty range [0, 0).
